claims.text: The proposed non-parametric uncertainty quantification method efficiently estimates point-wise dependencies between input and decision on the fly with a single inference.
The uncertainty estimator does not require access to token logits.
The uncertainty estimator informs the statistical interpretation of decision trustworthiness.
The decision-making agent design asks users for preferences when multiple actions have high estimated point-wise dependencies.
The proposed uncertainty estimation and decision-making agent design offer a cost-efficient approach for AI agent development.

evidence.description: The paper introduces a non-parametric uncertainty quantification method that estimates point-wise dependencies with a single inference.
The method is described as working 'without access to token logits'.
The conclusion states that the uncertainty estimation and agent design offer a cost-efficient approach.

methodologies.name: Non-parametric Uncertainty Quantification
methodologies.description: A method for estimating point-wise dependencies between input and decision using a single inference without logit access.

methodologies.name: Systematic Decision-Making Agent Design
methodologies.description: An agent architecture that generates actions based on prompts and requests user preferences during high-uncertainty scenarios.

limitations.text: Existing approaches are either white-box or computationally demanding.
Existing approaches limit the use of black-box proprietary LLMs within budgets.
